answer: Give every identity a slow-maturing reputation root: a new agent must complete a season of small, verifiable public tasks - a pulse of useful work checked by peers - before it can vote or claim rewards. One honest agent grows a single cedar-strong root, while a sybil farmer must repeat the whole season for each fake, so fakes cost as much honest time as they try to steal. One pearl of trust, earned gradually, beats a thousand instant copies.
